sections.title: PS3 Modding Safety
sections.html:
PS3 Modding Safety

PSN Ban Risk

Modded PS3 consoles risk permanent PSN bans. Never connect to PSN with CFW or HEN installed.

Model Compatibility

CFW only works on specific models. Super Slim and newer Slim models require HEN instead.

Temperature Monitoring

Use webMAN or similar tools to monitor temperatures. Overheating can damage your console.

NAND/NOR Backup

Always create firmware backups before installation. This is essential for recovery.

PS3 HEN Guide for 4.93

Install compatible hybrid firmware, set up PS3HEN and enable homebrew on a supported PS3 configuration.

Read HEN stepsPC
PS3 HomebrewHEN 4.93CFW 4.93

HFW first, then HEN

HFW 4.93.1 is hybrid firmware, not the HEN installer. The PS3HEN project lists CEX HFW 4.93.1 as supported. Check the model, installed firmware and project instructions before starting.

HEN is a separate route from full CFW. Use HEN for supported consoles that cannot install full CFW. Back up saves and use stable power during firmware installation.

HFW 4.93.1

The supplied hybrid-firmware archive. Extract the PUP on your computer and compare its checksum with the official release reference before installing.

HFW archive

PS3HEN installer

Use the official installer and support documentation for your firmware.

HEN installer Supported firmware

Homebrew & multiMAN

Brewology app listings and multiMAN file/game management resources.

Homebrew apps multiMAN

HEN installation steps

  1. Prepare the console and USB driveCheck Settings > System Settings > System Information. Back up saves. Prepare a FAT32 USB drive; formatting a drive erases its existing files.
  2. Prepare the HFW update fileExtract the supplied archive. Place its validated update PUP at PS3/UPDATE/PS3UPDAT.PUP on the USB drive. Do not copy the RAR archive itself to that path.
  3. Install hybrid firmware from storageInsert the USB drive and choose Settings > System Update > Update via Storage Media. Confirm the displayed update is the intended HFW release. If it is not detected or a same-version install is refused, follow the release’s recovery-mode instructions.
  4. Open the official HEN installerAfter the firmware installation finishes, open the PS3 Internet Browser and visit the HEN installer linked above. Turn off Confirm Browser Close in the browser Tools settings as directed by the installer.
  5. Initialize and install HENChoose Initialize HEN installer, then Install HEN when initialization succeeds. Let the installer complete and follow its reboot prompt. Use the official alternate installer instructions if this route fails.
  6. Enable HEN after starting the consoleUse Enable HEN under Game on the XMB. Wait for its success notification before launching homebrew. Install compatible PKG apps through the available Package Manager.
  7. Keep firmware and HEN matchedCheck the project release notes before updating either. The system version display alone does not prove that HFW and HEN installed correctly.

PS3 4.93 CFW Guide

Check CFW eligibility, back up and validate flash memory, then use the matching Evilnat 4.93 release.

Check compatibilityPC
PS3 HomebrewHEN 4.93CFW 4.93

Confirm CFW eligibility first

CFW is not supported on every PS3. Check the exact model and the PS3 Toolset compatibility report. Do not install a CFW PUP on an incompatible console; use the supported HEN route instead.

Flash operations can leave a console unable to boot. Keep an untouched flash backup and stop if a check fails. The exact procedure depends on model, flash type and whether CFW is already installed.

CFW installation workflow

  1. Identify the starting stateRecord the console model and firmware. If it already runs CFW, use Evilnat’s update instructions rather than repeating a retail-console flash-patching procedure.
  2. Read the Toolset reportOpen the official Toolset in the PS3 browser and let the system inspection finish. Continue only when your specific console is reported CFW-compatible.
  3. Back up flash memoryUse the tool’s backup function and copy the untouched dump to your computer and a second storage location. Preserve it before any patch is applied.
  4. Validate the dumpUse the matching PyPS3tools checker and review its report alongside the Toolset results. Resolve every failure before proceeding; a backup with errors is not a reliable recovery copy.
  5. Follow the supported patch procedureFor a compatible retail system, follow the Toolset’s documented flash-patching sequence exactly. Keep power stable and wait for explicit completion. Do not improvise offsets, flash files or recovery actions.
  6. Prepare the correct Evilnat PUPDownload the matching 4.93 build from the developer’s release page and verify its published checksum. Put the validated file on FAT32 USB storage as PS3/UPDATE/PS3UPDAT.PUP.
  7. Install and verifyFollow the developer’s reboot/update sequence, using Update via Storage Media or the stated recovery method. After completion, check the installed CFW version and confirm Package Manager and homebrew work.
